item: The Wikidata item fetch and the place resolver are registered as writers: they commit to the corpus, and the flag's one consumer (the offline maintenance hold-off) now sees them (R360)
summary: wikidata-items (store_items commits WikidataItem rows) and resolve-places (resolve_mentioned commits Place rows every thousand and at the end) were registered with is_writer=False under a comment whose premise was wrong: the flag would not ask the operator to stop a collection pass, because that ask reads _DB_WRITER_KINDS in api/jobs.py, which neither job is in and which this change does not touch. The flag's one consumer is offline_maintenance (it skips the whole maintenance window while a writer job runs; checked when a tick starts and between passes), so the whole maintenance window (counter reconcile, orphan prune, language reconcile, incremental vacuum, the hourly snapshot) could run beside either job. Both are now True. The guard is an AST inventory of every BackgroundJob( in src/ pinning the set of non-writer kinds exactly, with one reason each: a new job registered without the flag fails until its module is read, and flipping either job back fails the inventory. Red-before: two of three tests fail on the old flags (the inventory-sees-the-jobs control passes on both). STATED LIMIT: this does not change the restore. The restore never reads the job registry (WAL's R359 grep: no is_writer or all_job_statuses in src/backup), so a restore's exposure to these two jobs is the restore lane's question, not answered here. STILL OPEN: ai-coordinator also commits (perception and translation sweeps) but is a loop that stays running while its setting is on, so a True flag would hold maintenance off indefinitely; it is recorded in the test as an open decision, not flagged (R362).
